See the technique on tagging for more on this. Upgrading the child is about upgrading those beliefs with new information about your present day reality. It further allows you to stop acting out of the fear and limiting beliefs that your childhood brought about. You don't live there anymore. You live in this new upgraded reality. You were taking compassionate responsibility for your childhood self and assuring them that things will be different now and that now they are safe. The client is invited to bring their childhood self into their adult life where they don't have to be subjected to the pain and abuse of their early life. Here is what it sounded like with Daniel. Marissa and I want you to imagine taking that baby home from the hospital and into your lovely home with your partner. I want you to imagine installing that little boy into your own world. In your world, you're not the runt. You don't compete for attention. You don't need your mother to meet your unmet needs anymore. You have friends and adult partner and your sons. So every time you look at needles and blood now, you don't have to remember your unmet needs and that scared little boy because that isn't you anymore. It's nothing more than a dim memory that doesn't now and never again will influence you. Merging the child The final step completing the trio with the last two techniques, merging the child represents total healing. Sit down and imagine that child version of yourself at an age when you felt the most vulnerable. Feel that child dropping down into your present day self, starting at your head and traveling down, merging into your body, head, heart, soul and mind. You can say to that child, I've created a place in my heart and life for you. I've created a place in my body for you. You belong to me now. You live in my world and now that you live in my world I don't have to go back and live in your world ever again. Instead of constantly feeling like an overlooked unwanted kid, you visualize putting that kid into your grown-up body. From now on you are free to act and react like a smart, lovable adult who matters, who is enough, who is significant. That damaged child doesn't exist anymore. Raise you've always wanted. People can go their entire lives hoping to hear praise from a particular person or figure in their life. Thinking that it will make up for the praise they may not have received as kids. But it doesn't work. In fact, praise that comes from ourselves is often more powerful and lasting because our minds have to believe it. When you need a boyfriend, girlfriend, husband, wife, child or boss to love you in order to make you feel loved and valued. The risk is that even if you find it it may not last. After all, marriage is end. Children grow up and find their own partners and bosses can fire you. The best insurance policy is realizing that you don't have to seek praise from external sources. Teaching people to replace the harsh, hurtful words or storylines they've internalized. With ample and regular praise they can give themselves is transformative. I do this in RTT by having the clients say out loud all the words they have needed to hear for so long and giving them a recording that has those keywords and phrases in it. Repetatively listening to those words through a recorded audio will imprint on the subconscious and change a person's internal dialogue in a permanent and meaningful way. You can use these techniques on yourself even when you're not in hypnosis or in the presence of a therapist. You can provide love and affirm your value to yourself throughout your entire life no matter what is happening externally every single day. All you have to do is think of the words you've always wanted to hear from others. Usually they're all the same. I'm lovable, I'm significant, I'm worth it, I'm matter. Say and think these words as much as possible. Speak them out loud in front of the mirror each morning. Set them as your phone locks green. Say them in your head. Create a recording of them you can listen to. When you give yourself the praise you've always wanted through sustained repetition of these affirmations both internally and out loud. You are meeting your unmet needs and filling up the missing part of you. You think of the words you've always wanted to hear and the praise you've always wanted and give it to yourself regularly and repeatedly. Don't give someone else the job of making you feel better when you can do it so well yourself. Tagging Children are very good at forming fixed beliefs. When something bad happens or when there is a chronic repeating problem at home they think I can't change this. It will always be this way. There is nothing I can do about it. I call this tagging or attaching a fixed belief to a passing phenomenon. So if a child is in poverty they tag it as there will never be enough food I'll always be wanting. If the parents can't provide love to a child the child will always think there's nothing I can do about this I'm just unlovable. It's understandable why children do this. After all they can't go out and get a job to bring home money nor can they change the way their parents treat them. However what happens is that these tags we attach to life tend to stick around. The conditions of our childhood turn into what we think is destiny. I'll always be out of shape I'll always be broke. I'll never find true love. We have the option to take these old beat up tags from childhood and replace them with new ones rip off that tag and tell yourself something better. Don't reduce your adult experience to how things were for you as a child. Notice what your tags are and try and connect them to beliefs you may have formed as a result of your childhood. Then you can begin to create new ones. Ladder of looping thoughts. Imagine a ladder with five rugs. The first run is a thought. I'm not enough. The second run is a feeling that comes from that thought. I'm not enough so I feel sad, depressed, hopeless, angry, etc. The third run is the action and behaviors that come from thinking that thought and feeling it. Often that action is no action. Nothing ever works out so I won't apply for that dream job. The fourth run is a behavior that is the sum total of your actions and in actions. Nothing ever works out. I sabotage everything. I don't deserve anything so I just don't even try. Finally, the fifth run is how you justify all this by looping back to the initial thought. I'm not enough. This pattern is what I call a looping thought. It can be a hugely destructive force that starts with a simple corrosive thought and it can ruin your whole life. But on the flip side, a looping thought pattern when applied positively can change your life. Imagine you formed a new looping thought. I am enough. So the next run is I feel brave. I feel good about myself. I feel able to take risks. The third run is an action. I'm going to ask that person out. I'm going to apply for that position. The fourth run is behavior. I make things happen in the world. I go after what I want. And finally, all of that is justified and reinforces the fifth and final run. I am enough. So remember that a thought becomes a feeling, a feeling becomes an action. An action becomes a behavior. A behavior justifies itself by looping back to and strengthening the initial thought. Use this pattern to your advantage by drawing the ladder and writing on each run, starting with a positive thought, thereby creating a positive loop. The three ways the mind works. When trying to change your behavior, it's hugely helpful to have a basic framework of how the mind works. I believe there are three guiding principles. The first one is that the mind does what it believes we want it to do. Your mind bases this entirely on what you've told it through your speech and repeated thought patterns. So if you want to change how you're behaving, tell your mind better things. I want this. I am ready for this. I can do this. Let your mind know with clarity what you want and don't focus or dwell on what you don't want. Your mind does what it thinks you want it to do. If you've got it wrong, that's because you've given it wrong information. The good news is you're able to fix that at any time. The second thing about the mind is that it responds to the pictures we form and the words we say. And we are free to change that. Make your pictures big and bold. Make your words evocative and relevant. Say what you want in the present tense and regularly imagine your wildest dreams coming true. The more you do this, the more your mind will respond and move you towards your desired reality. The third thing about the mind is that it likes what is familiar and resists what is unfamiliar. The good news about that is that you can make anything you like familiar with a little bit of repetition. After a week of making your coffee without sugar, the taste will become routine. If you exercise regularly, you will begin to dislike it when you skip a day. Keep saying to yourself, I'm making this good thing familiar and making this unwelcome habit unfamiliar. I love the motto, say it, state it, do it. And remember, you get to choose what to make familiar and what to make unfamiliar. PPP Often our problems can seem overwhelming and like they're running our lives. But the truth is that problems can only overtake us if they are what I call the three P's. Permanent, personal and pervasive. When you apply this framework to your problems, you'll find that there aren't many problems that satisfy all three categories. For example, if you can't find a partner, is that permanent? No, you can find one in the future. If your kid is driving you crazy, is that permanent? No, they will soon grow up and one day you'll miss them. If your boss is horrible to you, is that permanent? No, you won't have this job forever. Similarly, none of those problems are personal either. If your boss is mean to you, it probably means they hate everyone, not just you. Every teenager is difficult with their parents, that's not personal. If it isn't personal, you can begin to see ways you might solve it instead of feeling wounded and that it's all about you. Finally, those problems aren't pervasive either. They are not gripping your every waking minute preventing you from living your life or surviving. Your boss or teenage child is not affecting you when you are making love with your partner or having a nice dinner. By reframing our problems with the three P's, we can begin to regain some perspective on what's bothering us instead of drowning in it. Most importantly, we can take proactive steps to solve it. The Rules of Your Mind While this is the first time in this book I've laid them out explicitly, the Rules of Your Mind have played a role in every story included in this book. For years they formed the basis of my understanding of how to heal people and by extension are the bedrock of RTT itself. I learned these rules over many years from my clients and as I said before, my clients have taught me that the mind is not nearly as complicated as we are led to believe. Using these rules of your mind as the basis for your understanding of how people heal is crucial. 1. Your thoughts form a blueprint that your mind and body work to make a reality. Every thought you think causes a physical reaction and an emotional response. So be aware of your thoughts and be ready to change them. Science has proven that our beliefs and outlook have an effect on our immune systems and our ability to heal ourselves. Every clinical drug trial has to exclude the placebo effect because the belief or expectation that we will heal is sometimes even more powerful than the drugs themselves. Your mind does not care and indeed does not know if what you tell it is true or false, useful or useless, beneficial or harmful. It acts on words as if they are the absolute truth, so you may as well tell your mind better things, you will find yourself with better results. 2. The strongest force in humans is that we must act in a way that consistently matches our thinking. If you say, I am so stressed I know my skin is going to break out or gosh I am running late, my irritable bowel is going to act up and make me even later. Then that is exactly what will happen. Your mind must get you to act in a way that matches your thinking, so you must be very careful about what you present to your mind. Why? Because it is going to present it right back in your actions and external reality. 3. The subconscious is not good at future pacing, our subconscious functions better when it is working in the now. Rather than saying, I will find love, wealth, health or success next year. You must say, I am becoming wealthy, lovable, successful or super healthy right now on this day, in this moment. Saying that will mean your mind will begin to find opportunities and openings to match that reality. 4. Your mind responds to the pictures you form in your head and the words you say to yourself. This is actually great news because you can change those words and pictures any time. Ever notice that the more you try to avoid thinking about something the more it pops into your head. Don't think of chocolate is more or less saying to your brain, think of chocolate. Instead, create an alternative image that is evocative, compelling and alluring. And tell your brain to think of that. A delicious bowl of fruit with nuts and seeds sprinkled on top, full of seasonal and ripe fruits that will boost your immune system, instead of an artificial chocolate bar you'll inhale in 30 seconds. Fixate on that, and your mind will forget about the chocolate entirely. 5. The subconscious mind responds to words that are vivid, exciting, descriptive and in the present tense. When coming up with words and pictures, it's important to remember that your mind likes simplicity. The words and images you conjure for yourself should be direct, bold, affirmative and in the present tense. Don't temper your statements with qualifying words like maybe, eventually, try or someday. Don't speak in the future or past tense. Don't be wishy-washy or modest with the images you conjure. Be direct, precise and prescriptive. 6. The mind learns by repetition. This rule is so simple it almost feels like it can't be true, but it is. Athletes and musicians practice their craft or skill every day, because it builds neural pathways that make much of what they do automatic. A process known as neuroplasticity. The same goes for the more mundane thoughts and habits we create in our lives. If you tell yourself over and over, nothing works out. I can't do that. This will probably end in tears. Your mind learns to accept and even creates that reality. This rule is true for both good and bad thoughts. Just as you can unwittingly teach yourself negative habits through repetition, you can unlearn them and teach yourself positive ones through repetition. 7. Your mind cannot hold conflicting beliefs. When you have conflicting beliefs they cancel each other out. I have seen contradictions like this so many times in my office throughout my career. Often the client isn't even aware of them. They sound like, I want a baby, but I will lose my job and get fat. I want to speak in public, but everyone will laugh at me and I'll fail. I want love, but it would kill me if I got dumped again because it hurt so bad the last time. In these cases our mind is confused. It cannot pick a lane. However, when our mind is unidirectional, it becomes like a powerful laser. You'll never meet a vegan who loves bacon. They think it's disgusting. Their mind is clear. They're not fighting to refuse meat. When we present the mind with conflicting beliefs we unravel and unpick these beliefs until they cancel each other out, meaning we don't get the outcome we want. Your mind's job is to move you toward pleasure and away from pain. This rule is hugely responsible for keeping human beings alive. When you experience pain your mind searches for the cause and says never again. However, if you have an adverse experience such as a miscarriage an embarrassment while giving a speech at work or a shameful experience around food as a kid, your mind can easily attach pain to the wrong things. Things you actually want, such as having a baby, public speaking or eating and nourishing and healthy diet. It's important to make sure your mind isn't confusing pleasure and pain based on old or adverse experiences that are no longer relevant to you. You have to make the things you want pleasurable and the things you don't want painful. 9. What is expected tends to be realized? People underestimate the extent to which their expectations end up shaping their reality. This can happen in both implicit and explicit ways. In other words, it not only shapes people's interpretations of events, it can actually be the cause of certain outcomes. One example of this might sound like, I knew I'd get sick just like my dad. I saw my father taking medication every day for the ulcer he got, and I formed a belief that hard work makes you sick. That person then goes on to get sick from overwork. This rule is especially true for parents to keep in mind because children learn what they live. 10. In a battle between emotion and logic, emotion always wins. This rule is entirely central to RTT as you've probably realized by now. Most therapy is logical. Let's talk about what happened. Why does it make you feel that way? But when all problems and behaviors have emotional problems at their core, logic is a waste of time. If we could help people logically, we'd merely have to say, you are ruining your life without the whole. You should stop. Or you're a six foot tall grown man. You don't need to be afraid of something as small as a mouse. But those approaches simply don't work. If emotion defeats logic, forget about the logical explanation and work to change the emotion attached. 11. Your mind does what it thinks you want it to do. Your mind is doing what it thinks you want. Likely based on information you told it a long time ago in the form of your repeated or inherited thoughts. Your mind always thinks it is acting in your best interest. So if you're not getting the outcomes you want, give your mind better instructions. Remember, your mind does not care if what your talent is good or bad, healthy or not, true or false. It doesn't care if you tell it you want to eat potato chips or apples. Work on your project or procrastinate, go for a walk or watch more Netflix. Like putting lotion on your skin, whatever you tell it, it lets in. Give your mind relevant, detailed up to the minute instructions so your mind doesn't act on old or unhelpful information. 12. Your mind is hardwired to resist what is unfamiliar and return to what is familiar. One of the most damaging things we can tell ourselves or think is, that's not available to me. Whether it's love, money, career success or weight loss, we have to make the things we want familiar. Even if we didn't grow up with any of those things, we can tell our minds that the things we desire are deeply familiar to us and make the things we want to leave behind entirely unfamiliar. Our mind is wired to do the rest because it loves to stay with what's familiar. 13. The greater the conscious effort, the less the subconscious responds. In a battle between the subconscious and conscious, the former will always win. That's why simply saying to yourself, try to go to sleep or try to relax, never works. It's also why the harder you try to have an orgasm, the harder it becomes. If you take away the conscious effort, you leave room for the subconscious to take over. Stop trying and instead give your subconscious better instructions. Sleep comes to me. My body is a fat burning machine. My digestion is amazing.
